nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe2/CC shows diffraction peaks at 29.79°, 33.40°, 36.70°, 42.67°, 50.48°, 55.20°, 57.52°, 61.88° and 72.20° corresponding to (200), (210), (211), (220), (311), (023), (321), (400) and (421) planes of cubic pyrite NiSe2 (ICDD PDF card No.41-1495). Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC shows decreased NiSe2 peak intensity with no Ni(OH)2 peaks, indicating amorphous Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of NiSe2/CC and Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC. In the XRD patterns of NiSe2/CC, all the diffraction peaks at 29.79°, 33.40°, 36.70°, 42.67°, 50.48°, 55.20° 57.52°, 61.88° and 72.20° can be assigned to the (200), (210), (211), (220), (311), (023), (321), (400) and (421) crystalline surfaces of cubic pyrite of NiSe2 ... After electrodeposition of Ni(OH)2, the intensity of NiSe2-related diffraction peaks decreases while no peaks of Ni(OH)2 are detected, indicating the possible formation of amorphous Ni(OH)2 on the surface of NiSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe2/CC shows uniform vertically textured nanosheets consisting of smooth small nanoparticles. Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC maintains vertical nanosheet morphology but with rougher surface due to amorphous Ni(OH)2 coverage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of as-prepared samples was then analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM; Fig. 1 b-c). As seen in Fig. 1b, uniform and vertically textured NiSe2 nanosheets covering the entire CC substrate were obtained ... Fig. 1c shows the sample of Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC. It can be clearly seen that the morphology of the vertical nanosheets is almost unchanged after electrodeposition of Ni(OH)2. However, after carefully observing one nanosheet with higher magnification inserted in Fig. 1c, we find the smooth surface of the nanosheet is becoming more rough after electrodeposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2/NiSe2 shows thin amorphous Ni(OH)2 layer on NiSe2 core with lattice fringes of 0.238 nm corresponding to (211) plane of NiSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image taken from the Ni(OH)2/NiSe2 confirms a thin layer of amorphous Ni(OH)2 deposited on NiSe2 (Fig. 1g). In addition, the core demonstrates the lattice fringes with the interplanar spacing of 0.238 nm corresponding to the (211) plane of NiSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC contains Ni, Se, and O elements with homogeneous distribution across nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum (Fig. S4) ensures the existence of Ni, Se and O elements in as-obtained Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC, and the EDX elemental mapping images of Ni, Se and O indicate the fairly homogeneous distribution of the constituents across the nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 at 855.8 eV and Ni 2p1/2 at 873.5 eV (spin-energy separation 17.7 eV) indicate Ni(OH)2 phase. Se 3d peaks show negative shifts vs NiSe2/CC suggesting strong electron interactions. O 1s at 531.1 eV (OH groups) and 532.6 eV (adsorbed water/O2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Ni 2p region ... the binding energies (BEs) at 855.8 and 873.5 eV ... correspond to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2. The spin-energy separation between the two Ni 2p peaks is 17.7 eV indicating the existence of Ni(OH)2 phase. The peaks for Se 3d in Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC show negative shifts compared with those of NiSe2/CC ... in O1s regions, the peak at 531.1 eV is considered as oxygen in OHe groups, and the peak at 532.6 eV can be attributed to adsorbed water or possibly adsorbed O2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC Cdl = 50.5 mF cm^-2 vs NiSe2/CC Cdl = 15 mF cm^-2, indicating enlarged active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC reveals a Cdl of 50.5 mF cm^-2, which is higher than that of NiSe2/CC (15 mF cm^-2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC shows Rct of 1.182 Ω at -200 mV overpotential, lower than Ni(OH)2/CC (96.58 Ω) and NiSe2/CC (4.998 Ω), indicating fastest electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni(OH)2/NiSe2/CC electrode shows a lower Rct (1.182 Ω) at overpotential of -200 mV (Table S1), which is smaller than that of Ni(OH)2 electrode (96.58 Ω) and NiSe2 electrode (4.998 Ω).
